people.gloss: Flying clouds (Vương Bột: họa đống triêu phi Nam Phố vân)
people.role: Hall-mistress of Nam Phố Đường since 1100; the west's talisman maker
people.appearance: A slight woman with ink-grey fingertips and her hair pinned with a brush, who rises before the birds and has not missed a dawn in two hundred years.
people.backstory: Châu Phi Vân was born in Tang Ma Thành in 930 among the mulberry and hemp, and at four drew her first talisman in mulberry juice on a hemp rag (A199). The founder Nghiêm Họa Đống (nghiem_hoa_dong) took her at eight and taught her to paint the morning cloud. In 1097, not yet mistress, she found that the ink-grinder Sào Ẩn Lan (sao_an_lan) had darkened at the Jade Milk spring, gave her a year's stones and sent her up the karst, and told no one. She has kept the hall since 1100. Its scribes held the prize seal of the talisman contest at Hạc Đinh Thị for eleven contests, until a girl of fourteen from Lạc Hà, Tô Mộ Vân (to_mo_van), took it in 1190 (A203). Châu was glad. She has asked the lord twice to lend her the girl for a season, and this spring she asked for the placed boy Tạ Quy Yến (ta_quy_yen) by name; Lạc Hà's envoy Hách Ánh Hà (hach_anh_ha) kept him off the thirty contracts for her, and the hall owes the envoy a favour. In 1173 the hall painted a hundred fire talismans on a Lạc Hà order for clearing the reed beds at Thủy Khẩu. Châu painted the master sheet herself. Lô Xướng Vãn's (lo_xuong_van) raiders burned Lãng Đào's boats at Đào Sa with them (A080). She has painted no fire talisman since, and the hall's loyalty to its lord has not recovered. This year she fills the lord's war orders with Đới Huyền Nghiên's (doi_huyen_nghien) dark sheets, which she knows are darkening him as they darkened Sào, and pays him by the sheet.
people.wants: To meet the lord's war orders without painting another fire talisman, and to paint the whole Painted Beams talisman once, dawn and dusk together, before she dies.
people.secret: Every year since 1175 she has sent Lãng Đào's head Giang Cửu Khúc an unsigned bundle of ward talismans for his rebuilt ferries, stamped with no seal. Lạc Hà's enemy's boats sail under her wards. She has also 'lost' four of Lạc Hà's war orders since the Ferry War; her elder Kha Triêu Phi keeps a record of them and has told her that a fifth sends it to the Vassal Hall.

people.role: First elder; head of the dusk line and the hall's dealings with Lạc Hà
people.appearance: A handsome, grey-temple scholar in a dusk-violet robe a shade too close to Lạc Hà's, who quotes Vương Bột in every second sentence.
people.backstory: Kha Triêu Phi was born to a family of failed examination scholars in Phong Lâm Trấn, among the maples the Lạc Hà founder planted (A190), and grew up looking up the river at the great sect's hall. Ôn Châu Liêm (on_chau_liem), the founder's partner, took him as his last disciple in 1055 and taught him the dusk half of the founders' art, the half that rolls up the western hills' rain. Ôn died at Châu Liêm Trấn in 1060 with most of the dusk half still in his head. Kha has kept the dusk line since, and keeps the hall's accounts with Lạc Hà. He likes Lạc Hà, and it likes him. In 1173 he took the Counting House's order for a hundred fire talismans and wrote 'for the reed beds of Thủy Khẩu' on the order slip himself. He watched the hall's loyalty fall after Đào Sa (A080) and thinks Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van) has cost the hall a century of trade over a fire it did not light.
people.wants: To bring the hall back into its lord's favour, by Châu's war orders or by her fall, and to take the prize seal back from Lạc Hà's prodigy at the next contest.
people.secret: He knew what the fire talismans were for. The Boat Hall's master Lô Xướng Vãn told him in 1173, and Kha wrote the reed beds on the slip so that Châu would paint them. He keeps a record of the four war orders she has 'lost', copied by his scribe Doanh Mộ Vũ, and has told her that a fifth sends it to Lạc Hà's Vassal Hall; he would keep the hall for its lord after her.

people.role: The hall's champion scribe; lost the prize seal to Tô Mộ Vân in 1190
people.appearance: A tight-mouthed woman of fifty with a callus on her brush finger the size of a pea.
people.backstory: A Hoa Khê girl who won the talisman contest at Hạc Đinh Thị twice for the hall, and in 1190 lost it to a fourteen-year-old from Lạc Hà, Tô Mộ Vân (to_mo_van), in front of the whole market (A203). She has painted the same cloud talisman every dawn since, some three thousand sheets. She took it badly that her mistress Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van) then asked to borrow the girl. Her ruler has cracked the knuckles of Tạ Quy Hồng (ta_quy_hong), who now paints in gloves, and she has not asked him whether it hurts.

people.role: Ink-grinder at the Jade Milk spring; paints the hall's dark talismans at night, paid by the sheet
people.appearance: A pale, careful man who smells of wet stone and wears gloves to keep the ink off his skin, and lately to keep it in.
people.backstory: A Hầu Đầu Thôn mushroom-picker's son from the karst, Kha Triêu Phi's (kha_trieu_phi) disciple, he grinds the hall's ink in the Jade Milk spring among the stone pillars, where the water carries a dark qi. For ten years the talismans painted with his ink have held longer than any others; for three they have come out a shade darker each season. A thread of Darkness has woken in him, and the whole hall knows it. Since the spring Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van) has had him paint Lạc Hà's war orders at night in the ink-house, where the dark takes best, and pays him by the sheet.

people.role: Keeps the hall's talisman stall at Hạc Đinh Thị
people.backstory: A Phương Thảo mat-weaver's daughter and Kha Triêu Phi's (kha_trieu_phi) disciple, who sells the hall's talismans below Lạc Hà's old seat and hears everything the Counting House clerks say over lunch. She prices by the buyer's face, and sent Văn Tang Chỉ (van_tang_chi), the hall's own paper master, away from the stall for sneezing, so the hall's paper went unsold that day.

people.role: The hall-mistress's youngest disciple; writes talismans on petals
people.appearance: A round-faced girl of sixteen with petal stains on her sleeves and a habit of humming while she paints.
people.backstory: In Hoa Khê lovers drop their names into the brook on the spring petals (A194). At ten Lý Khê Thư wrote a name on a petal so well that it would not sink, and the couple it named came to the hall to complain. Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van) took her that day. She paints at dawn like her mistress and has asked twice to be taught the dusk half too, which no one at the hall can teach her.

people.role: Outer disciple who paints the stern-lamp talismans for Vãn Đăng's boats, in the dark ink
people.backstory: A Vãn Đăng fisher boy whose village lights its lamps on the dusk of 803 but does not put out (V104). He carries Đới Huyền Nghiên's (doi_huyen_nghien) ink down from the spring, and since last year he has painted his own village's stern-lamp charms with it, because they hold three times as long. His hands are grey to the wrist.

people.backstory: A Phong Lâm scholar's daughter who painted the clouds of the southern shore at dawn and found the paintings held qi. In 880 she and Ôn Châu Liêm (on_chau_liem) founded the hall under Lạc Hà (A198) on the forest shore below the old seat. She wrote the canon in the margins of her paintings and died at dawn in 1100 with a brush in her hand, leaving the hall to Châu Phi Vân (chau_phi_van).
